panels.title: The divisions before the walls
panels.desc: The headland city walled and besieged: divisions camped on the heights around it, each general's tent flying its own banner, messengers riding the roads between.
panels.scene: High three-quarter view of Paxos's besieged headland city, walled on its peninsula with the sea on two sides. On the heights around it, separate divisions are camped at a distance from one another, each general's tent flying a different banner. Lone horseback messengers ride the winding roads between the camps, and out on the water a hostile squadron holds the seaward approach.

panels.title: The siege
panels.desc: The walled headland city at dusk, encircled at a distance by separate camps, each with its own general's tent and banner; messengers ride the long roads between.
panels.scene: The walled headland city on its peninsula at dusk, encircled at a distance by the separate camps of the besieging divisions; each camp has its own general's tent flying a different banner, and lone horseback messengers ride the long roads between the camps.
panels.caption: THE DIVISIONS WERE CAMPED ALL AROUND THE CITY. THE GENERALS COULD SPEAK TO ONE ANOTHER ONLY BY MESSENGER.

panels.title: The bribed general
panels.desc: Inside a lamp-lit tent at night, a cloaked go-between hands a general a purse of gold; he is already dictating conflicting orders to two scribes at once.
panels.scene: Inside a lamp-lit general's tent at night, a cloaked figure from the besieged city hands a purse of gold coins to a general, who is already dictating to two different scribes at once: one scribe draws a crossed-swords symbol (attack) on a tablet, the other draws a retreating-footprints symbol.
panels.cast: the bribed general, a go-between, two scribes
panels.caption: THE BRIBED GENERAL NEED NOT REFUSE TO FIGHT. HE NEED ONLY TELL THE LEFT FLANK ONE THING AND THE RIGHT FLANK ANOTHER.

panels.title: Two betrayals, one view
panels.desc: A split panel: a loyal commander betrayed by a lying lieutenant, and a treacherous commander relayed honestly — from Lieutenant 1's seat, identical.
panels.scene: A split panel with a vertical divider. Left half: a loyal commander gives a crossed-swords tablet to Lieutenant 1 and the same to Lieutenant 2, but Lieutenant 2, shifty and shadowed, whispers a retreating-footprints tablet to Lieutenant 1. Right half: a shifty commander hands a crossed-swords tablet to Lieutenant 1 and a retreating-footprints tablet to an honest-faced Lieutenant 2, who passes it on to Lieutenant 1. Lieutenant 1's pose and the tablets he holds are identical in both halves.
panels.caption: TWO DIFFERENT BETRAYALS — AND FROM WHERE LIEUTENANT 1 STANDS, THEY LOOK EXACTLY ALIKE.

panels.title: The Illyrian generals
panels.desc: A general bends over a campaign map crowded with painted figurines, moving a whole cluster of them at once with both hands, like a puppeteer.
panels.scene: Inside a general's tent, bent over a large campaign map covered with many small painted wooden figurines of foreign generals in distinctive tall helmets; he moves a whole cluster of figurines at once with both hands, like a puppeteer.
panels.caption: EACH OF THREE GENERALS PLAYS THE PART OF A THIRD OF THE ILLYRIAN ARMY.

panels.title: The oral relay
panels.desc: Four hilltop camps around a valley: a commander sends three messengers to three lieutenants, who then relay to each other; one sorts three tablets, two matching and one odd.
panels.scene: Four hilltop camps around a campfire-lit valley: a commander on the highest hill sends three messengers down to three lieutenants' camps; the lieutenants then send messengers across to each other. In the foreground, Lieutenant 2 sits at a camp table sorting three wax tablets into a pile of two matching ones and one odd one out.
panels.caption: FOUR GENERALS, ONE TRAITOR: LIEUTENANT 2 HEARS “ATTACK”, “ATTACK”, AND ONE LIE — AND TAKES THE MAJORITY.

panels.title: The same seal, twice
panels.desc: A lieutenant holds two wax tablets side by side in torchlight — one attack, one retreat — both bearing the same commander's seal.
panels.scene: Close-up of a lieutenant in a bronze helmet holding up two wax tablets side by side in the torchlight: one shows a crossed-swords symbol, the other a retreating-footprints symbol, and both bear the same large red wax seal with the commander's eagle emblem. His eyes are wide with realization.
panels.caption: THE SAME SEAL ON TWO DIFFERENT ORDERS. ONLY THE COMMANDER COULD HAVE MADE BOTH — SO THE COMMANDER IS THE TRAITOR.

panels.title: The broken roads
panels.desc: Bird's-eye over the siege lines: camps joined only by certain passes and bridges; some roads end at collapsed bridges, forcing long detours.
panels.scene: A bird's-eye mountain landscape around the besieged headland city: the generals' camps are joined only by certain narrow passes and bridges; several roads end at collapsed bridges over ravines, and messengers must take long detours through other camps.
panels.caption: NOT EVERY CAMP COULD REACH EVERY OTHER. SOME ORDERS HAD TO PASS THROUGH OTHER GENERALS’ HANDS.

panels.title: The marginal lamp
panels.desc: On a warship's deck at night, a failing signal lamp guttering at half strength; two helmsmen disagree on whether it is lit.
panels.scene: An illustrative scene, not tied to a place on the island. At night on a trireme's deck, a single signal lamp hangs from a pole, its flame guttering at half strength. Two helmsmen stare up at it: one points and gestures 'lit!', the other shakes his head 'dark'.
panels.caption: NO ROPE OR BRONZE CAN SAVE YOU: A FAILING LAMP CAN LOOK LIT TO ONE HELMSMAN AND DARK TO THE OTHER.
